chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: Fats gets him back; why Fats called him Hymie
summary: Fats couldn't stand it and made Kirkeby call Hermie back; the nickname Hymie came from a girl in Philadelphia calling for him, and Fats picked it up.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: So what -- well, this -- we're getting ahead of our story, up -- to get up the Neverly, but when you came all -- finished with Claud Hopkins band, this was back in the thirties again, and Fats had been --
No, oh you mean the big band. Claud's band.
Claud's big band, yeah, and Fats -- you would have been hearing Fats from the Panther Room, while you were with --
And -- well, did Fats finally get you back? What happened?

Yes, I had to -- he couldn't stand it any longer, and he made Kirkaby, and everybody else, call me to get Herman back, you know. And I was glad and he was glad, and we were happy. We united, and -- Oh Hymie! Hymie, it's so good to see you! Like that.
Why did he call you Hymie?
Well Fats started calling me that.

Well, I don't know that -- let me see, what happened? We were in Philadelphia, and some girl I knew came into the hotel somewhere and asked for me, or called me, Is Hymie -- Hymie! You know. Because Herman -- Hymie, in

Jewish, you know, think it's Herman, and Hymie, and Jewish name, Chaim, and all that, the same. So they started calling me Hymie! And Fats picked it up. He started calling me Hymie and on a lot of the recording dates, Hymie! I said what do you want?
So I used to get a lot of mail, Hymie.
Yeah, uh-huh. And still do, here and there, once in a while, get a letter, card, or something. Hymie, you know?
